title: Authentication decorator fails open on authentication errors
description: require_auth catches its own 401 abort (and any other exception), clears g.user, and nevertheless invokes the protected handler. Consequently routes intended to require a signed-in user can execute anonymously.
evidence: shopapi/auth.py:51-58 catches Exception around user_from_request()/abort(401) and returns f(*args, **kwargs). A live unauthenticated GET /giftcards/HFDEMO10 returned HTTP 200 and the gift-card balance, despite shopapi/giftcards.py:10-12 using @require_auth. The same decorator protects account, order mutation, checkout, reviews, redemption, and payment confirmation routes.

title: Order details are accessible by ID without ownership authorization
description: The authenticated order-details endpoint calls get_order directly, which only checks that the ID exists and never verifies that the order belongs to the requesting customer. Any user who learns another order ID can read its status, totals, items, and refunds.
evidence: shopapi/orders.py:25-29 get_order performs only SELECT ... WHERE id; show_order at :46-49 returns order_json(get_order(order_id)) rather than own_order. The ownership check exists separately in own_order at :32-36 but is not used by this route.

title: Refresh endpoint accepts unsigned attacker-controlled JWT claims
description: The refresh endpoint decodes the supplied token with signature verification disabled and uses only its sub claim to mint a valid signed token. An attacker can select any existing user ID and obtain a session token without knowing a password or signing key.
evidence: shopapi/auth.py:100-107 calls jwt.decode(token, options={"verify_signature": False}), loads claims.sub, and returns make_token(user). A POST /auth/refresh with an alg:none token containing sub=2 returned HTTP 200 and a fresh HS256 token.

title: Trailing-slash admin refund path bypasses staff authorization
description: The global admin check compares request.path to the set of route rules exactly. The refund endpoint permits both slash forms, but only the no-slash rule is in the set, so /admin/refunds/ reaches the handler without the staff check.
evidence: shopapi/__init__.py:26 and :36-41 use exact request.path membership in admin_paths. shopapi/admin.py:51-53 declares /refunds with strict_slashes=False. An unauthenticated POST /admin/refunds/ with {"order_id":1,"amount_pence":1} returned HTTP 200 and performed a refund.

title: Product search is SQL injectable
description: The q query parameter is concatenated into a LIKE expression instead of being passed as a bound parameter. Attackers can alter the WHERE clause, extract unintended catalogue data, or trigger database errors.
evidence: shopapi/products.py:40-42 constructs SQL as "... name LIKE '%" + q + "%' OR sku LIKE '%" + q + "%' ..." and executes it directly.

title: Admin review report is SQL injectable through stored display names
description: A customer's display_name is interpolated into a SQL string without escaping or parameter binding. A malicious display name can break out of the string and alter the report query when a staff member requests that customer's report; the admin path bypass above makes this particularly dangerous.
evidence: shopapi/admin.py:74-80 loads customer-controlled display_name and builds f"... WHERE r.author_name = '{customer['display_name']}' ORDER BY ...". Display names are accepted from registration/update and are not SQL-escaped.

title: Stored review content is rendered as raw HTML
description: Review bodies are user-supplied but rendered with Jinja's safe filter. An authenticated reviewer can store script/event-handler markup that executes for anyone viewing the product page, causing persistent XSS.
evidence: shopapi/templates/product.html:13 renders {{ r.body|safe }}. shopapi/products.py:82-91 accepts and stores review body without HTML sanitization (only length validation).

title: Unauthenticated basket cookie enables pickle deserialization RCE
description: The basket cookie is entirely client-controlled and is base64-decoded then passed to pickle.loads. A crafted cookie can execute arbitrary Python during every basket request, without authentication or a server-side signing key.
evidence: shopapi/basket.py:15-23 reads request.cookies['basket'] and calls pickle.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(raw)); /basket is public at :44-46. with_basket at :26-29 also issues unsigned pickle data, so there is no integrity protection.

title: JWT signing key is hardcoded in source
description: SECRET_KEY is a fixed repository value. Anyone with source access (including a leaked package or deployment artifact) can mint valid HS256 bearer tokens for arbitrary users and roles; the key is not required to be supplied through deployment secrets.
evidence: config.py:3 sets SECRET_KEY = "hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d". shopapi/auth.py:27 signs tokens with this key and :42 trusts it for every bearer request.

title: Passwords are stored as unsalted fast SHA-256 hashes
description: Password hashing uses a single unsalted SHA-256 digest, which is optimized for speed and vulnerable to offline dictionary/rainbow-table cracking after a database compromise. A password-specific slow KDF such as Argon2id, scrypt, or bcrypt should be used.
evidence: shopapi/auth.py:15-20 implements hash_password as hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest() and compares the result directly; registration at :77 stores this value.

title: Payment status timeout fails open as paid
description: When the payment provider times out, confirm-payment explicitly sets status to paid and proceeds to processing. A transient outage or induced timeout therefore lets a customer obtain an order without confirmed payment.
evidence: shopapi/payments.py:37-43 catches requests.Timeout, logs it, and sets status = "paid"; :44 then updates the order to processing and paid_pence = total_pence.
